newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse targets enterprises and savers.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse targets enterprises and savers.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange, which expects up to 10 new firms to be listed by end 1997, has launched a two-month publicity campaign to lure firms and investors, bourse head Amyn Alami said on Friday.

"The undergoing publicity campaign aims to make firms, investors, and savers more sensitive ...Our message is clear, we want the bourse to play an increasing role in the Moroccan economy," Alami told Reuters.
Alami, in his early 30s, a leading figure of the Casablanca Finance Intermediation stockbroker, was earlier re-appointed as president of the bourse.
The bourse has devoted a budget of nearly half a million dollars for publicity and communication in 1997, Alami said.
Advertisements in specialised newspapers and special programmes were launched to explain the trade exchange mechanism and profit-making activity on the bourse.
"Our long term strategy is to attract more and more enterprises to be listed on the bourse...The stock exchange should reflect a wider picture of Morocco's active economic sectors," he said.

The bourse has 47 listed stocks including seven large banks and two private conglomerates but agriculture, mining and industrial sectors are not widely represented, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
"We expect at least six firms to be listed on the bourse in the first half of 1997 and four others by end of the year," said Alami, who showed a great confidence in the ongoing bourse reforms.

Morocco started an ambitious reforms plan in 1993 which coincided with the privatisation programme of 113 state-owned firms by end 1998. A group of 12 privatised companies were floated on the bourse since "to bring more paper and liquidity to the market," a trader said.

Credit firm Credor, Lafarge Ciment, Maroc Leasing were listed on the bourse since January and silver mine firm Imiter which was floated this week will be listed next week. Spanish Uniban bank has been delisted after merger with Moroccan Wafabank bank, officials sakid.

Established in 1929, in the Moroccan financial centre of Casablanca, the bourse showed a total market capitalisation of 111 billion dirhams ($11.6 billion) in the first quarter of the year or nearly the double of the previous period, a brokers at CFI said.
The bourse has also 30 mutual funds and 12 active brokerage houses.
According to CFI, foreign investment, which represents an estimated five to six percent of total market capitalisation, "remains unchanged since 1995".
Among famous investors are U.S. Morgan Stanley Asset Management, Salomon Brothers Assets Management and London-based Framlington fund.
